oracle.description: This file is the single normative lifecycle oracle. The accompanying Markdown files are checked views and rationale, not a second model.
oracle.transitionExpansion: A transition whose source is an array expands to one identical transition per listed atomic source configuration. @source in stoppedActors expands to the invokedActors of that source. @target in startedActors expands to the invokedActors of the target.
oracle.eventSelection: For one dequeued event, evaluate transitions from the active atomic state in listed priority order. Take the first transition whose guards all pass. If no state transition passes, apply globalEventPolicy.
oracle.checkedViewRule: Every checked-view global-policy row must equal its globalEventPolicy oracle object in all five fields: id, ordered events, literal when condition, ordered actions, and literal result. Every checked CleanupCertificate, CleanupTerminalFault, terminal-contract, cleanup-terminal discriminant, slot-lifecycle, retention-bound, and churn row must likewise equal its named oracle object. Omitting an action column, paraphrasing GEP04/GEP05/GEP06, widening a cleanup terminal category, or copying a partial certificate/fault field inventory is a projection failure.
oracle.actionOrder: Installed XState 5.32.5 orders a selected external transition as source exit actions, transition actions, target entry actions, target invoke input evaluation, source fromCallback disposal or fromPromise abort notification, then target invoke start. Every possibly surviving resource is therefore covered before acquisition/start by either its own deduplicated release slot or the exact P3-C07 queue subtree's one parent-owned composite slot. beginOrPromoteCleanup revokes acquisition, captures the complete immutable source-tree snapshot, and creates the selected immutable phase snapshot in its transition action; a disposer or abort handler can only trigger an existing idempotent release. Slot retirement may delete registry entries only after terminal evidence reaches every referencing snapshot.
oracle.versionRule: Only advanceVersion changes context.version. Ignored, stale, duplicate, rejected, and idempotent no-op events leave it unchanged. Public observations are ordered by version only when their required incarnationId values match; different incarnations are unordered.
oracle.terminalActorRule: Every actor terminal event is emitted only after its own handles release and every acquisition-time release-slot terminal settles. The exact P3-C07 queue subtree is covered transitively by one parent-owned composite slot whose release is exact queue.stop() and whose terminal adopts that exact promise; the frozen queue and private job receive no registry capability and register no separate slots. cleanupBarrier is a per-invoke bounded fromPromise over a frozen registry phase terminal. Both terminal events carry the one exact CleanupCertificate type; the error terminal additionally carries the one exact CleanupTerminalFault type. Admission requires current invoke plus exact epoch/phase/lease/effective-scope/certificate/audit identity, the frozen release-set identity, and zero live or unresolved resources. The cleanup actor boundary admits only permanent/invariant terminal categories and totally normalizes every authentication/transient/unknown internal failure to the fixed safe invariant cleanup-terminal-contract fault after certified settlement. Malformed/invalid certificate material remains inside that boundary pending authoritative certification and never becomes a fromPromise rejection. Watch-to-workflow promotion always installs a fresh workflow phase terminal before replacement invocation. Slot retirement cannot erase phase evidence or allow a new acquisition to reuse a settled closure.

reservedActorEventBoundary.rule: The public/trusted external send adapter parses only externalSendEventIds and has no constructor or escape hatch for any actor-origin or xstate-origin terminal event. Every reserved-prefix value and every event whose oracle origin is an actor or xstate is rejected before actor.send. Only XState may construct invoke terminal events with its non-forgeable actor identity.
reservedActorEventBoundary.modelInjection: A pure transition-selector test may construct reserved terminal material to prove that invalid certificate guards select no modeled transition/action and map to GEP05. It must not call actor.send with that reserved event or claim XState runtime ignore semantics; bypassing the boundary with an actual unhandled xstate.error.actor event can put the root snapshot in status error and is a conformance violation.
reservedActorEventBoundary.mechanicalCheck: Require the four control.* externalSendEventIds to exist with origin control-service, lifecycle.restart.requested and process.shutdown.requested to exist with origin daemon-supervisor, and credentials.changed to exist with origin credential-owner; require every xstate.done.actor.* and xstate.error.actor.* event to be absent. Parse every known event through the external schema: exactly the seven allowed IDs pass and all 17 internal/reserved events fail before actor.send.

cleanupTerminalFieldSetClosure.structuralCheck: Resolve CleanupCertificate.* to the authority's exact leafFields. Both terminal event references and every consumer reference must resolve to that same type. Every ordered guardAndPolicyReads leaf must exist in the authority and therefore in both terminal contracts; duplicates, extra, missing, renamed, or separately enumerated terminal fields fail.

typescriptImplementationObligation.type: type CleanupTerminalFault = Readonly<{ category: 'permanent' | 'invariant'; code: string; safeMessage: string; releaseCertificate: CleanupCertificate }>
typescriptImplementationObligation.schema: One strict discriminated schema accepts exactly the four named fields, errorCodeSchema-compatible code, safeErrorMessageSchema-compatible safeMessage, the literal permanent|invariant category union, and the exact CleanupCertificate schema; authReason and every extra field are rejected.
typescriptImplementationObligation.boundary: cleanupBarrier's fromPromise implementation catches every unknown synchronous/asynchronous failure inside the actor logic. It never directly rethrows an unknown or broad WorkflowFault. It awaits or requests the registry's certified zero-audit phase settlement, then strict-parses the complete terminal and returns CleanupCertificate success or throws exactly the parsed CleanupTerminalFault. A permanent/invariant certified fault is parsed and retained; authentication/transient/unknown material is converted by the total non-throwing normalizer to the fixed invariant fault above. A malformed or invalid certificate/terminal parse never rejects into XState: the adapter keeps or resumes the authoritative registry wait and may reject later only after a valid certified terminal exists. If no CleanupCertificate exists yet, the actor remains pending on registry settlement and does not reject.
typescriptImplementationObligation.noPublicWidening: CleanupTerminalFault is internal actor-terminal authority only. Public status/control/error-envelope schemas and their six registered public error codes are unchanged; recordTerminalFailure projects only the already accepted bounded sync.terminal-failure diagnostic.

globalPolicySeparation.GEP03: Only an exited-invoke or duplicate terminal identity; it is never a category fallback.
globalPolicySeparation.GEP05: Only model-injected current terminal material with an invalid CleanupCertificate; it is never a category or exited-invoke fallback. A conforming actor boundary never emits this material into XState.
globalPolicySeparation.currentTypedError: A current first error carrying a valid certificate is structurally permanent/invariant and must take exactly one local transition.

cleanupTerminalDiscriminantClosure.mechanicalCheck: Require exact equality of the ordered admitted literals in CleanupTerminalFault.discriminant, faultIsFatal.acceptedCategoryLiterals, actor errorType, event error payload type, and every cleanup-error transition guard. Expand T145/T171/T183/T185 and require each of the 13 cleanup states exactly once. For each state and each admitted category, an installed XState 5.32.5 fromPromise rejection with a valid current certificate must select exactly one modeled terminal transition and leave root snapshot.status active or done, never error. Authentication/transient raw inputs must normalize to the fixed invariant fault before rejection. Actual stale old-invoke rejection must be ignored through XState actor identity under GEP03. Invalid certificate material must fail strict parsing and remain pending inside the actor boundary; a pure selector injection selects no transition/action and maps only to GEP05. Never actor.send a reserved terminal event or describe that bypass as an XState ignore guarantee.

Atomically call resourceRegistry.requestPhase(targetState.minimumScope) during the transition action. First revoke every acquisition capability in the exiting source ownership tree, capture one immutable complete source-tree snapshot, select the eligible set of release slots registered before resource acquisition/start including any one parent-owned P3-C07 composite queue slot, and create the immutable phase snapshot/release-set identity. Registration after this first freeze is structurally unavailable. Then: if no session, increment cleanupEpoch and cleanupPhase and create it; on every cleanup-state entry increment cleanupInvokeLease; on watch-to-workflow promotion increment cleanupPhase and install a fresh immutable workflow phase over the broader subset of the source-tree snapshot before returning even if the watch phase already settled; on equal/narrower scope retain the phase and expose its pending/cached terminal through a new per-invoke promise. A composite queue trigger calls exact queue.stop() once and its slot terminal adopts that promise. Retired slots contribute snapshot-owned immutable evidence, not a registry lookup. Retain scalar epoch/phase/lease/slotGeneration high-water marks so later terminals and identifiers are stale. The terminal event retains its own immutable certificate for following actions. This is the only final cleanup owner.

releaseSlotProtocol.register: Except for the exact frozen P3-C07 queue subtree covered by compositeQueueSlotProtocol, before an actor or descendant acquires/starts each external resource it synchronously calls registerReleaseSlot(ownerScope, ownerInvokeIdentity, resourceOrdinal, stableResourceId, release). The registry allocates one never-reused slotGeneration, creates slotInstanceId=<incarnationId>:<slotGeneration>, and immediately creates one pending terminal. The exact unretired acquisition key deduplicates only callers for that same resource acquisition. Registration completes before the resource becomes live or externally reachable; a failed acquisition settles and retires that same slot.
releaseSlotProtocol.capabilities: Direct-resource acquisition code receives a register capability only while its owner source tree is active. initialBackfill or recurringSweep uses that parent capability once to pre-register the P3-C07 composite slot, but the exact queue and private job receive only their frozen adapter/request/capacity inputs and never receive the registry or any register/trigger capability. A disposer or AbortSignal handler receives only triggerRelease(slotId). The first requestPhase synchronously revokes every register capability in the exiting source ownership tree and freezes the eligible covering subset; later promotion can select a broader subset only from that same already-registered tree. The type/state boundary exposes no register operation after the first freeze.
releaseSlotProtocol.trigger: triggerRelease is idempotent and may run from requestPhase, fromCallback disposal, fromPromise abort, normal completion, or descendant shutdown. Every caller addresses the same slot and same terminal; no caller creates a close promise.
releaseSlotProtocol.settle: A slot terminal settles success or error exactly once after the owned handle is closed/removed. Release error is diagnostic material, not permission to skip the remaining slots. The terminal yields immutable SlotTerminalEvidence before registry retirement. A phase terminal cannot settle until all phase-local frozen terminal references have yielded evidence and the phase-local authoritative audit reports zero live and zero unresolved resources.
releaseSlotProtocol.descendants: All descendants use direct acquisition-time slots except the exact frozen P3-C07 queue subtree. For that sole exception, initialBackfill or recurringSweep owns one parent composite slot before queue construction; the queue and private rawDownloadJob register nothing, receive no registry capability, and own no separate job/listener/response/staging slots. The parent workflow terminal awaits the composite queue.stop() terminal.
releaseSlotProtocol.lateRegistration: Impossible by construction: JavaScript cannot interleave requestPhase with synchronous registration, requestPhase revokes the only register capability before freezing, and source disposer/abort closures never possess it. An implementation exposing registration to disposal/abort violates I21 before runtime.
releaseSlotProtocol.capacityAdmission: Registration first resolves an exact unretired acquisition-key deduplication without allocating an identity or acquiring another resource. For a new key, if retained slotEntryCount equals configuration.maxReleaseSlotEntries, registration returns WorkflowFault {category:transient, code:sync.release-slot-capacity, safeMessage:Release-slot capacity exhausted.} before allocating an identity, invoking release, acquiring a resource, or changing the live/unresolved audit. The actor follows its typed fault path and cleanup covers only entries that already exist.
releaseSlotProtocol.generationAdmission: After deduplication and capacity admission for a new key, the registry allocates slotGeneration as a monotonically increasing positive safe integer. It never wraps, resets, or reuses the value inside an incarnation. If allocating the next generation would exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, registration returns WorkflowFault {category:invariant, code:sync.release-slot-generation-exhausted, safeMessage:Release-slot generation exhausted.} before identity allocation or resource acquisition; the incarnation follows terminal failure.

slotLifecycle.identity: slotInstanceId is <incarnationId>:<slotGeneration>. slotGeneration is registry-allocated, monotonic, positive, and never reused. stableResourceId remains diagnostic/audit metadata; the P3-C07 value remains rawDownloadQueue:<parentInvokeIdentity>:0. A new resource always receives a new generation even if its stableResourceId text repeats.
slotLifecycle.deduplication: Only the exact unretired acquisition key {ownerScope, ownerInvokeIdentity, resourceOrdinal} can return its existing slot handle. This lookup precedes new-slot capacity and generation admission and allocates or acquires nothing. The key is single-resource and capability-bound. Retirement revokes it. An old key or handle can only observe its captured settled terminal; it cannot address a new slot, and a new acquisition cannot deduplicate onto an old settled terminal or release closure.
slotLifecycle.normalOrAcquisitionFailureLinearization: When a slot that no cleanup snapshot references settles normally or as acquisition failure, the registry atomically creates immutable SlotTerminalEvidence, updates live/unresolved counts, appends at most one bounded safe diagnostic, and revokes the acquisition key and registry trigger handle. The terminal-settled to retired transition linearizes at deletion of the slot entry in that same turn; only then may the owning actor terminal or a replacement acquisition proceed. No tombstone or release closure remains in the registry.
slotLifecycle.phaseReferencedLinearization: When a slot referenced by the immutable source-tree snapshot or any open, promoted, settled, or cached phase settles, the registry atomically creates immutable SlotTerminalEvidence; resolves the already-captured terminal reference in the source-tree snapshot and every referencing phase snapshot; creates replacement immutable phase audit/diagnostic records; and revokes the acquisition key and registry trigger handle. The terminal-settled to retired transition linearizes at deletion of the slot entry in that same turn. Any phase that becomes complete then creates its immutable success/error terminal from its own records. No phase performs a later slot-map lookup.
slotLifecycle.oldHandleAfterRetirement: The acquisition owner may retain a local settled promise until its actor terminal. Repeated trigger calls return that same local settled result and never consult the registry. Actor terminal/cancellation drops the handle. Registry entry count and dedup state remain zero for that retired slot.
slotLifecycle.retirementAuthority: Only the registry performs terminal-settled to retired. There is no actor-visible unregister, purge, delete, revive, or reuse operation.

immutableSnapshots.sourceTree: The first requestPhase atomically revokes acquisition and captures one immutable source-tree snapshot containing every then-unretired covering slot's slotInstanceId, stableResourceId, ownerScope, immutable terminal reference, and diagnostic seed. Later promotion selects from this snapshot even after corresponding registry entries retire.
immutableSnapshots.openPhase: Each new phase is one immutable value {cleanupEpoch, cleanupPhase, effectiveScope, ordered frozen slot references, frozenReleaseSetId, terminal}. The ordered release set and identity never change. Equal/narrower replacement creates no phase; it creates only a new invoke wrapper/lease over this value.
immutableSnapshots.settledPhase: Settlement atomically replaces the open value with one immutable settled value that additionally owns every SlotTerminalEvidence, bounded diagnostics, authoritativeAudit, certificateId, and success/error terminal. Cached wrappers and GEP05 read only this value, never retired registry entries.
immutableSnapshots.promotion: At most one watch-to-workflow promotion creates a fresh immutable workflow phase from the source-tree snapshot. It retains the prior watch phase as the sole superseded snapshot until finishCleanupScope, so open or cached watch evidence remains byte-identical while the current workflow certificate is independent.
immutableSnapshots.independence: Slot-entry retirement cannot change a current, cached, promoted, or equal-scope certificate because terminal evidence, ordered release-set identity, diagnostics, audit, certificate ID, and terminal outcome are snapshot-owned values.

retentionBounds.slotEntries: 0 <= slotEntryCount <= configuration.maxReleaseSlotEntries <= 4096. Only registered/release-triggered/terminal-settled-during-the-current-atomic-linearization entries count; retirement deletes each entry and release closure in the same turn.
retentionBounds.sourceTreeSnapshots: 0 when no cleanup session is open; exactly 1 after first requestPhase until finishCleanupScope. It contains at most maxReleaseSlotEntries terminal references/evidence records.
retentionBounds.phaseSnapshots: 0 when no cleanup session is open; otherwise at most 2: one current phase plus at most one superseded watch phase. Equal/narrower replacement allocates no phase snapshot. Each phase contains at most maxReleaseSlotEntries terminal references/evidence records.
retentionBounds.cachedPhases: A settled current phase is cached only until literal certificate admission and finishCleanupScope. A superseded watch phase is retained only until the same finish. No prior cleanup session phase is retained afterward.
retentionBounds.finishCleanupScope: After the current CleanupCertificate is admitted, atomically close the session and drop its source-tree snapshot, current/superseded phase snapshots, cached terminals, audits, and diagnostic evidence. The terminal event retains its own immutable certificate, so a following appendCleanupDiagnostics action can copy bounded diagnostics after the purge. Exited invoke events carry their own immutable values and are rejected by XState identity.
retentionBounds.total: At every instant, registry-owned slot entries plus source-tree/phase terminal-reference records are at most 4 * maxReleaseSlotEntries <= 16384; the one source-tree plus at most two phase envelopes add at most 3, so total retained registry/session units are at most 16387. Incarnation churn changes only scalar epoch/phase/lease/slotGeneration high-water marks.

compositeQueueSlotProtocol.owner: The active initialBackfill or recurringSweep parent invoke owns exactly one workflow-scoped registry slot for its exact frozen P3-C07 queue subtree.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.input: registerReleaseSlot receives ownerScope=workflow, ownerInvokeIdentity=<parentInvokeIdentity>, resourceOrdinal=0, stableResourceId=rawDownloadQueue:<parentInvokeIdentity>:0, and one idempotent release closure capturing a queue variable that is unbound until construction. The registry adds its never-reused slotGeneration. The exact queue constructor still receives only the production download adapter and positive capacity.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.linearizationPoint: The parent synchronously registers rawDownloadQueue:<parentInvokeIdentity>:0 before constructing the queue, then constructs and binds the exact queue in the same JavaScript turn in which neither XState nor requestPhase can interleave. If construction throws, the parent settles that already-registered slot as an acquisition failure before propagating the fault.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.releaseTrigger: The slot's idempotent trigger calls exact queue.stop() once after binding. All requestPhase, parent abort, and normal-completion callers address this same trigger; none constructs a second close job.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.terminal: The registry slot terminal aliases/adopts the exact promise returned by queue.stop(); it is not a parallel wrapper close. The terminal settles with that promise only after the queue reaches stopped.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.auditIdentity: rawDownloadQueue:<parentInvokeIdentity>:0 plus its registry slotGeneration is one member of the workflow phase frozen release set, participates once in frozenReleaseSetId, and contributes one liveResourceCount/unresolvedReleaseCount unit until the exact queue.stop() promise settles. The accepted stableResourceId text and queue API are unchanged.
transitiveProof: Queued P3-C07 jobs hold only request/deferred/flags and no acquired external handle; stop rejects each queued promise synchronously.
The one active P3-C07 fromPromise job owns an AbortController; stop aborts it and waits for its terminal event.

The active invoke awaits adapter.download and its finally removes the caller abort listener; the frozen production adapter fulfills or rejects only after its response close/error, awaited staging, and its own finally cleanup.

The queue enters stopped and resolves stop waiters only after the active invoke settles, so the exact queue.stop() terminal transitively covers the private job, listener, response, and staging cleanup without separate registry slots.
compositeQueueSlotProtocol.capabilityBoundary: The exact P3-C07 queue source/API remains unmodified: its constructor input is adapter plus capacity, its job input is request plus signal plus adapter, and neither level receives the registry, a registry capability, or a slot identity.

requestPhaseLinearization: The first request revokes every acquisition capability in the exiting source ownership tree, captures the one immutable complete source-tree snapshot, selects the eligible covering subset of its pre-registered direct slots plus any parent P3-C07 composite queue slot, creates the immutable phase snapshot and frozenReleaseSetId, and triggers each selected slot idempotently before source disposal/abort can run. Broader watch-to-workflow request: before replacement invoke creation, atomically select the broader subset of the immutable source-tree snapshot, including terminal evidence for already-retired members and any workflow composite queue slot, set workflow, allocate phase+1 and lease+1, install a fresh pending immutable workflow phase over that union, reuse/deduplicate only still-live release triggers, and run a fresh snapshot-local workflow audit. No acquisition capability is reopened. This rule is identical for open and settled watch phases.

finishCleanupScope: only after literal CleanupCertificate admission, close the session and purge its one source-tree plus at most two phase snapshots; the event-owned immutable certificate remains available to following actions, and later cleanup allocates a new epoch.
cleanupProtocol.phaseSettlement: Only the registry may settle a phase. The immutable phase snapshot already owns its effective scope, ordered frozen release set, release-set identity, and terminal references. It awaits every reference even when one rejects, replaces the open snapshot with an immutable settled snapshot containing every terminal evidence/diagnostic/audit fact, and creates a CleanupCertificate success or CleanupTerminalFault error only at literal liveResourceCount=0 and unresolvedReleaseCount=0. A certified permanent/invariant release failure retains that category. Authentication/transient/unknown failure material is redacted and converted to the fixed invariant `sync.cleanup-terminal-contract` fault; no broad WorkflowFault rejection crosses the adapter boundary. A superseded phase may finish for its old wrapper but cannot mutate or settle the current phase. Retired slot entries are never consulted.
cleanupProtocol.invokeAdapter: Each cleanupBarrier fromPromise awaits resourceRegistry.awaitPhase(epoch, phase), which always returns a new promise for that invocation over the immutable phase snapshot. If the same phase is already settled, the registry resolves the new promise from its cached immutable terminal and the wrapper binds the current lease. It never reuses an old invocation output. If scope promoted, the wrapper awaits the fresh workflow phase, never the old settled watch promise. Slot retirement has no effect on either result.
cleanupProtocol.admission: Parse the success output or CleanupTerminalFault.releaseCertificate through the exact CleanupCertificate authority, parse every error through the strict CleanupTerminalFault authority, then require current XState invoke plus exact certificate/context/registry epoch, phase, invoke lease, effective-scope, and frozenReleaseSetId equality; scope dominance; audit scope and release-set equality; literal released=true; literal zero live and unresolved counts; and current immutable phase certificate/audit digest equality.
cleanupProtocol.invalidMaterial: Wrong scope, stale phase/epoch/lease, replaced invoke, wrong frozen release set, wrong certificate ID/digest, or nonzero live/unresolved audit cannot transition. Old-invoke events are ignored under GEP03. Malformed/invalid current material is caught before fromPromise rejection and remains pending on authoritative registry certification; a later valid terminal may use the fixed invariant normalization. A pure model-selector injection maps to GEP05 but is never sent to XState and is not a runtime-ignore claim.
